title: model_rebuild(force=True) must put mocks back, not delattr the validator/serializer/core schema
answers: model instantiation fails while another thread calls model_rebuild(force=True)
concurrent Model(...) during force rebuild uses the parent class validator
why does model_rebuild set mocks instead of deleting __pydantic_validator__
body:
Invariant: Code reads `__pydantic_core_schema__`, `__pydantic_validator__` and `__pydantic_serializer__` without holding the rebuild lock (for example when a model is instantiated). If you delete them from `cls.__dict__`, a concurrent read falls back through the MRO and can pick up the parent class's validator/serializer.
Enforced in: pydantic/main.py:BaseModel.model_rebuild. When the model is `already_complete` (force=True), it calls `_mock_val_ser.set_model_mocks(cls)` instead of `delattr`. This also keeps pydantic-core and schema generation from reusing the stale validator/serializer/schema.
If skipped: threads that instantiate the model during a forced rebuild intermittently validate with the wrong schema or fail. tests/test_freethreaded.py:test_model_force_rebuild_concurrent_instantiation covers this.
Constraints: Any future code that invalidates these class attributes should replace them with mock objects (MockValSer/MockCoreSchema via set_model_mocks) rather than delete them.
applies: pydantic/main.py model_rebuild and any code that invalidates model validator/serializer/core schema
